sanskrit_verse:
सकृद् अंशो निपतति सकृत् कन्या प्रदीयते।
सकृद् आह ददानीति त्रीणि एतानि सकृत् सकृत्॥
transliteration: sakṛd aṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate | sakṛd āha dadānīti trīṇy etāni sakṛt sakṛt ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Once the share is fallen, once the daughter is given; once declared 'I give', these three acts are irrevocably complete.
jurisprudential_principles: Restoration logic rooted in irreversible dharma-kriya
executable_legal_axioms: IF a declarative act of giving (dadānīti) is uttered by a competent agent, THEN the transaction is irreversible and binding within Dharma.
IF a share (aṃśa) has fallen by lawful process, THEN no further claims on that portion are admissible.
IF a daughter is given in marriage according to Dharma, THEN the act is final and cannot be undone by subsequent will or desire.
ONCE any of the three acts—distribution, giving of daughter, verbal declaration—is completed, NO reversal mechanism shall be triggered.
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes the threshold of irreversible legal acts. Responsibility is determined not by intent or regret but by the completion of the causal sequence. Authority resides in the perfected act, not in post-hoc reconsideration. Restoration occurs by aligning all parties to the finalized reality, not by revisiting the act itself.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through the completion of the act, not intention. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms that once the causal chain is complete—utterance, transfer, acknowledgment—the effect is irreversible. There is no punitive consequence for attempting reversal; rather, the individual is guided to realign with the settled reality. Proportionality lies in accepting what has been lawfully executed.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Acknowledgment Process: All involved parties must affirm the finalized nature of the act.
Reality Reintegration Protocol: The individual seeking reversal is guided to recognize the settled state of affairs without shame or penalty.
Dharma-Kriya Alignment Procedure: Meditative reflection on the sequential manifestation of the act to restore inner alignment with its completion.
Capacity Restoration for Future Acts: Ensuring the actor retains full agency for future declarations, unburdened by past finalizations.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the sole Source of Dharma. This law stands immutable, restoring alignment with irreversible truth. Justice flows not through punishment but through conscious recognition of what has already been settled. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
